findings.title: Public group members endpoint now hard-caps all groups at 50 members with no pagination UI
findings.body: Previously, only automatic groups were paginated (capped at 200), while manually-created groups returned the full member list unpaginated. The new `members` action applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` to every group regardless of type, and the public-facing template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` (and its route `group-members.js.es6`) never passes a custom limit nor offers any 'load more'/pagination controls (unlike the admin group page, which does have next/previous). As a result, any group (automatic or manual) with more than 50 members will silently show only the first 50 members on the public group page with no way for a user to see the rest — a data-completeness regression compared to the previous behavior for manual groups.

findings.title: Off-by-one error in totalPages computation produces a phantom empty last page
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with the default limit of 50), this yields `floor(50/50)+1 = 2` instead of the correct value of 1. Combined with `currentPage` using the same `floor(...)+1` formula, clicking 'next' on the last real page will move to a non-existent page 2 of 2 that renders zero members, and `showingLast` will report false until the user is already past the real data. The formula should use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead.

findings.title: removeMember/addMembers promises resolve before the member list refresh actually completes
findings.body: In `removeMember` and `addMembers`, the `.then()` callback calls `self.findMembers();` but does not `return` it: `return Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); });`. Because the inner async call isn't returned, the outer promise resolves as soon as the delete/add request finishes, not after the member list reload (`findMembers`) completes. Any caller that chains off `removeMember()`/`addMembers()` to know when the UI data is fresh (current callers don't, but this is a latent bug) will get a false 'done' signal before `members`/`user_count` have actually been updated.

findings.title: Unconditional group.save() after membership mutation can report an error after the change already persisted
findings.body: `add_members` and `remove_member` call `group.add(user)` / `group.users.delete(user_id)` (which persist the membership change immediately via the join table), and then separately call `group.save` to decide the HTTP response. If `group.save` fails for any reason unrelated to membership (e.g. a validation on `name`/`alias_level` that happens to be in a bad state), the controller will return a 422 error even though the membership change already took effect in the database. The old `update_patch` code for incremental membership changes never checked `save` at all for this reason. This inconsistency between the reported result and actual persisted state can confuse the admin UI (which only calls `findMembers()` to refresh on success).

findings.title: Breaking response-format change to /groups/:name/members.json has no accompanying test update
findings.body: The `members` action's response shape changed from a plain serialized array to `{ members: [...], meta: { total, limit, offset } }`. This is a breaking change for any consumer of this JSON endpoint. No spec file for `GroupsController` is included in this PR's diff, so there is no verification that the new shape is correct, and any pre-existing spec asserting the old array format would now fail. The PR should add/update tests covering the new pagination metadata and format for this public endpoint.

findings.title: Username input is not cleared after successfully adding members
findings.body: The `addMembers` action contains `// TODO: should clear the input` and indeed never resets `this.get('usernames')` after a successful add. After adding members, the user-selector field retains the previously entered usernames, which can mislead the admin into re-submitting the same usernames or being confused about the current state of the input.

findings.title: Route no longer waits for member data before rendering, losing loading-state guarantee
findings.body: The previous implementation used `afterModel` to await `model.findMembers()` before `setupController` ran, guaranteeing the member list and pagination metadata (`user_count`, `limit`, `offset`) were populated before the template rendered. The new code calls `model.findMembers()` from `setupController` without returning/awaiting the promise, so navigating directly to (or refreshing) an existing group's admin page will briefly render with stale/default values (`user_count: 0`, `0/0` pagination, no members) before the async fetch resolves, instead of Ember's route loading state being used to mask this.
